name: Garlicky Gochujang Tomato Bucatini

instructions.primary_message: For the Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until al dente, following timing on package's instructions. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.

While water comes to a boil, in a large skillet, combine oil and garlic and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until garlic is soft, fragrant, and just turning pale golden, 5 to 7 minutes. Add gochujang and cook, stirring frequently, until it loosens and darkens slightly, about 1 minute.

Stir in passata and salt. Bring a simmer and cook over medium-low heat until flavors meld and sauce slightly thickens, 8 to 10 minutes; lower heat as needed if sauce begins to bubble aggressively. Remove from heat until bucatini is ready.

Return tomato-gochujang sauce to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Add drained bucatini and 1/2 cup reserved pasta water. Stir until well-combined and sauce clings to the bucatini, about 1 minute. Season with salt to taste, if needed.
To Serve: Transfer pasta to serving bowls, top with a dollop of ricotta, black pepper, and basil leaves.

schema_metadata.keywords: tomato sauce, spicy tomato sauce, passata, spicy pasta, spicy bucatini, garlicky gochujang tomato bucatini recipe

description: This quick, easy pasta combines sweet garlic, silky passata, and gochujang for a savory, fiery sauce, finished with creamy ricotta and basil.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Ricotta, for serving; Freshly ground black pepper, for serving; Torn basil leaves, for serving

Notes: Passata is increasingly available in mainstream grocery stores, but it can also be found at specialty Italian markets and online. If unavailable, substitute 2 1/2 cups puréed canned whole tomatoes.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
